title: The docs for everything round 1 and round 2 changed
owns: README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/DEVELOPING.md, docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md, docs/RESEARCH.md and any other docs/**

items.title: README names a Windows 11-only microphone path for a supported Windows 10, and promises an Intel Mac artifact that a packages-only CI run doesn't make
items.scenario: (a) A Windows 10 22H2 user (README line 9 lists it as supported) follows README.md:84-85, "Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone › Let desktop apps access your microphone". That page doesn't exist on Windows 10, where it is Settings › Privacy › Microphone › Allow desktop apps to access your microphone. The merged code already gives both paths (WINDOWS_MIC_FIX, used by win32/system/doctor.ts and the setup check, review #100). (b) README.md:26-28 says a manual CI run with packages ticked keeps ember-packages, ember-windows, ember-macos and ember-macos-x64. ci.yml's macos-x64 job runs on dispatch only when `inputs.intel` is ticked too (ci.yml:723-725), so packages alone yields no ember-macos-x64. DEVELOPING.md §15 rightly says 'packages and intel'.
items.evidence: The Windows packaged doctor output in ci.yml run 40797546710 prints the both-versions fix text from WINDOWS_MIC_FIX. README.md:85 still has only the Windows 11 path. reports/platform.json forDocs asks for both paths at README.md:44. The macos-x64 `if:` is in ci.yml.
items.cause: platform #100's forDocs line wasn't applied at merge; the README Download text came from fix/docs
items.fix: README.md:84-85: give both paths, as WINDOWS_MIC_FIX does. README.md:26-28: say that ember-macos-x64 needs intel ticked too.
items.skeptic:
I could not refute either part. Both are confirmed in /home/user/wt/relfix-int, and both are minor documentation defects.

(a) Microphone path. README.md:84-85 gives only the Windows 11 path, "Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone › Let desktop apps access your microphone". README.md:9 lists Windows 10 22H2 as supported. The code knows the Windows 10 wording is different. app/main/environment.ts:320-325 defines WINDOWS_MIC_FIX with both paths, and its comment says "Windows 10 22H2 calls the page 'Privacy' and the switch 'Allow desktop apps to access your microphone'". The doctor (win32/system/doctor.ts:79) and the setup check (environment.ts:369) both use that constant. docs/DEVELOPING.md:752 also still has only the Windows 11 path.

The fix was requested and not applied. reports/platform.json forDocs (line 195) and the verifier note (line 307-308) ask for both paths at README.md:44 and DEVELOPING.md:731. The docs package ran in parallel and its report never mentions it. The merged diff of README.md leaves the microphone line untouched.

This is not a scheduled item. Neither "Open interaction notes" nor "Follow-ups after merge" in lead-notes.md lists it. Plan step 3 ("collect every report's forDocs lines; apply") has no commit in 63b88cd..HEAD.

The impact is limited. A Windows 10 user who runs the setup check or the doctor gets the right path; only the README text is wrong.

(b) Intel Mac artifact. README.md:26-28 says a manual run with **packages** ticked keeps ember-packages, ember-windows, ember-macos and ember-macos-x64. In .github/workflows/ci.yml:723-725, the macos-x64 job runs on workflow_dispatch only when `inputs.intel` is also ticked (and `only` is all or macos). Its upload step (ci.yml:809-812) sits inside that job. So a run with packages ticked and intel unticked produces no ember-macos-x64.

This is a regression against 63b88cd. The old README.md:60-61 said "(`ember-macos-x64` when **intel** is ticked too)". fix/docs replaced it with the new Download text and dropped that qualifier; README.md:28 is now the only place that names the artifact. docs/DEVELOPING.md §15 (line 1207) correctly says to tick both packages and intel.

items.title: DEVELOPING.md's GitHub CLI install line for builds without a client id doesn't work on RHEL 8
items.scenario: A developer on RHEL 8 (Ember's first platform), with a fork or a development build without a client id, follows 'Connecting Copilot': `sudo dnf install -y gh`. RHEL 8's repositories have no gh package, so dnf answers 'No match for argument: gh' and sign-in can't proceed. The repo's own source says RHEL 8 needs GitHub's repository: github-app.ts:33-36 GH_INSTALL.linux = 'sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo https://cli.github.com/packages/rpm/gh-cli.repo, then sudo dnf install gh'. Every sign-in message and the README (README.md:155-156) give that form. Commit 4e47b13 rewrote this paragraph for S1 and kept the wrong command.
items.evidence: The GH_INSTALL comment in app/main/agent/github-app.ts ('RHEL 8 needs GitHub's own repository'); README.md's RHEL 8 bullet; docs/DEVELOPING.md:203 unchanged in 4e47b13's hunk.
items.cause: pre-existing line kept by the S1 docs update (4e47b13; docs package)
items.fix: Replace line 203 with GH_INSTALL.linux's two commands (add GitHub's gh-cli.repo, then dnf install gh), as the README does.
items.skeptic:
Confirmed, but it is minor and the scenario overstates the impact. The defect: docs/DEVELOPING.md:203 still says `sudo dnf install -y gh      # or download from cli.github.com`, and that command fails on RHEL 8.

Evidence:
- The page's own scope (DEVELOPING.md:3) says §1–§9 cover RHEL 8.4, Ember's first platform.
- I asked Fedora's package source API for gh's branches (src.fedoraproject.org/api/0/rpms/gh/git/branches). It lists epel9 and epel10.x and f34–f45, with no epel8. Bodhi has 0 gh updates for EPEL-8. RHEL 8's BaseOS and AppStream don't carry gh either. So the command fails even with EPEL turned on.
- The same release adds app/main/agent/github-app.ts (new since 63b88cd). Its GH_INSTALL.linux at lines 33-36 says RHEL 8 needs GitHub's gh-cli.repo, and the README's RHEL 8 bullet (README.md:155-156) says the same.
- This is an unapplied hand-off, not just an old line. The agent package's report (reports/agent.json "forDocs") told the docs side to give the RHEL 8 form in DEVELOPING.md §Connecting Copilot: add gh-cli.repo with dnf config-manager, then dnf install gh. Commit 4e47b13 rewrote that paragraph for S1 and kept the old line as it was. The 4e47b13 diff shows line 203 as unchanged context.
- Neither lead-notes.md list ("Follow-ups after merge" or "Open interaction notes") schedules it. Their DEVELOPING.md items are only the #147 line at :131, More time to read, and remote.yml macOS.
- docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 has no accepted limitation that covers it.

Why it is minor:
- The line itself offers "or download from cli.github.com". A developer who gets dnf's "No match for argument: gh" still has a way through, so "sign-in can't proceed" is too strong.
- Only forks and builds without a client id are affected. The release build has the client id built in, and CI checks that id (device-code step green on bbe8ab2).
- The line was already there at 63b88cd (line 197), so it is not a regression. It is an incomplete docs follow-through of the agent package's hand-off.

Fix as proposed: replace the dnf line with GH_INSTALL.linux's two commands, as the README does.

items.text: Round 1's 21 packages each left lines for the docs (their reports' forDocs), and nobody applied them: the docs package ran at the same time. They are in specs/relfix2/partials.json (entries with id 'forDocs', per package), and the full reports are specs/relfix/reports/<package>.json (key 'final', field forDocs). For each line: check the current text on your branch (some may already be there, or the code may have changed since: read the code), then write it, in the docs' own style. List each line with done / already there / changed because <reason>.
This round's packages' forDocs lines are given in your task text. Same treatment.

docs/DEVELOPING.md: (1) the 'More time to read and answer' setting (Settings > Comfort & access): what it scales (every bubble's time ten times, a question's wait 20 minutes instead of 2, offers' 25 s) where DEVELOPING describes bubble timing; (2) remote.yml's macOS commands and SSH job now runs on every push (the repository is public, so runners are free), not only on dispatch or the weekly schedule; (3) #147: line ~131 says 'a failed card stays until you close it': replace with 'a failed card goes on its own after about a minute (the settings window's Conversation section keeps what went wrong)'.

docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §4.1 still names the switch '**Offer to bring Ember along when I connect with ssh**'; settings renamed it '…with SSH'. Fix the name (check app/renderer/home for the exact label).

CHANGELOG: add what the post-merge CI rounds fixed, for users: on Windows, Ember reads long lists and pages that are scrolled down (it reads what shows in full and leaves most of what is scrolled away out); on a German Mac, Ember finds System Settings as 'Systemeinstellungen'; a command window whose page crashes comes back with its commands instead of closing; if GitHub refuses Ember's sign-in request, Ember says so instead of showing a code of 'undefined'. Read the commits on ember-improve/20261027-release-fixes after 3d80b0c (git log 3d80b0c..bbe8ab2) for the exact behaviour.
